what_happened: Plan-time reading of lib/file-scope-overlap.sh showed session_contention() reads only .session_id/.task_numbers/.file_scope/.live/.liveness_reason, so the new queue entry schema can mirror those key names and reuse the predicate verbatim -- no edit to a shared multi-consumer library, and session_liveness() applies unchanged to a queue entry file.

Two research recommendations were deliberately narrowed at plan time: threading orchestration_id through every dispatch context was replaced by minting it inside queue-register and resolving later subcommands by session_id (D1), and scripts/command-gate-in.sh was dropped from the task's anticipated file_scope because the per-task acquire pass already covers single-task sessions (D6). Both are recorded as Decisions in the plan so implementation does not re-litigate them.

Phases 1-3 of the plan (queue-register/heartbeat/list, queue-finish/reap, queue-check) were implemented together in one editing pass rather than strictly sequentially, because write_queue_entry() is shared infrastructure all six queue subcommands consume; the consolidated test-task-lock-queue.sh suite still accumulates cases phase-by-phase as the plan directs, and each phase's own verification criteria were checked independently before closing it.

Phase 4's Tier Justification --only suite-selection run surfaced 5 NEW-looking failures (test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh). Verified via git stash push -- <the 3 phase-4-edited files> that all 5 fail identically on unmodified master, confirming they are pre-existing and unrelated to this task's edits; not investigated further as out of scope.
